title: A deep-learning pipeline to diagnose pediatric intussusception and assess severity during ultrasound scanning: a multicenter retrospective-prospective study.
summary: A deep-learning pipeline trained on 14,085 ultrasound images from 8,736 patients was evaluated on internal images and external videos. It achieved average AUCs of 0.972 for detecting three signs and 0.956 for classifying 184 videos. In a prospective 242-volunteer reader study, AI assistance raised junior sonographers’ average AUC from 0.857 to 0.966 and reduced median scan time from 9.46 to 3.66 minutes, similar to senior sonographers; patient outcomes were not measured.
ai_technology: A real-time deep-learning pipeline localized ultrasound signs and classified ileocolic intussusception and severity; prospective AI assistance was compared across sonographer experience levels.

evidence.tested: Primary abstract reports training on 14,085 images from 8,736 patients, internal image and external video evaluation, plus a prospective 242-volunteer sonographer study. Junior readers’ average AUC rose from 0.857 to 0.966 and median scan time fell from 9.46 to 3.66 minutes with AI assistance.
evidence.unknown: The reader study was a prospective pilot; it did not measure changes in treatment decisions, patient outcomes or sustained clinical workflow performance.
